checkpoint.goal: Make the animated contribution pasture feel cohesive, premium, and clearly readable in a GitHub profile README.
checkpoint.milestone: The accepted v22 champion publishes the complete pasture and two-section command panel as explicit GitHub light/dark assets while preserving contribution-scaled staffing, readable turnover, finish-aware pickup, and the full two-row roster.
checkpoint.last_verified: 2026-08-14: npm run check passed; the 991,941-byte fixture lasts 35.68 seconds. Forced 700x206 light and dark assets share one animation and render matching HUD palettes with separately framed selected-unit and 28-member roster bodies. A fresh independent Gate scored v22 19/20 with no blocker; profile publishing stages all three SVGs plus GitHub theme-context README URLs and runs immediately on a main source push.
checkpoint.next_action: Publish accepted v22 to main, observe the triggered profile workflow, and verify the public profile asset dimensions, panel, and theme-context README URLs.
approved_permissions: Read and write files inside this repository
Run local build, TypeScript, and credential-free SVG fixture commands
Write project research pages to the user-designated Obsidian vault

navigator.job: Own the visual outcome, checkpoint, permissions, resume, and final synthesis.

worker.job: Implement one bounded motion or rendering change and report its mechanical and visual evidence.

coach.job: Reproduce visual feedback and propose one causal task- or harness-level improvement.

gate.job: Independently compare a candidate with the frozen fixture, mechanical checks, permissions, and rollback guardrails.

feedback.observed: The pasture reads as assembled effects: too many sheep compete with the UFO, linear motion lacks weight, character acting is absent, and subpixel flowers and crumbs add clutter.
feedback.expected: A coherent miniature pasture with one clear UFO hero, four readable sheep actions, restrained secondary effects, and detail that survives at 700px.
feedback.evidence: Frozen 700px frames reproduce the clutter and flat motion, while source inspection shows a 40-sheep cap, zero-pixel drop descent, and linear per-effect animation tracks.
feedback.reproduction: The frozen 53x7 fixture scored 8/20 in docs/nulnul/visual-benchmark.md and rendered at 4,099,243 bytes with a sheep cap of 40 and per-particle keyframes.

feedback.observed: The replacement UFO shape is worse than the original, its hovering and banking feel cheap, eight sheep still feel dense, and the scene lacks speed.
feedback.expected: Restore the original UFO, use six sheep, and create a faster rhythm with brief acceleration and precise stops instead of constant floating.
feedback.evidence: The rejected fixture lasts 139.51 seconds, uses eight sheep, and adds continuous hover plus 3D bank transforms to a newly simplified UFO glyph.
feedback.reproduction: Inspect the rejected candidate at 700px around UFO entry, inter-drop travel, and grazing; compare the glyph with the repository's original UFO asset.

feedback.observed: The restored UFO keeps looking downward while it travels, and the pickup phase contains a long unintended drift instead of a clean wait and departure.
feedback.expected: Turn toward the next destination before departure, preserve that heading through flight, and remain fixed while waiting.
feedback.evidence: The v3 source forced every direction angle to zero, while the generated movement keyframes interpolated directly from the final drop at 12.63% toward the first pickup at 91.29% without a departure hold.
feedback.reproduction: Inspect the deterministic fixture at 700px during the first rightward flight and again at 60 seconds before the first pickup.

feedback.observed: The motion direction was proposed before studying established film, game-animation, game-feel, and web-motion methods, so the result remained a generic bundle of effects rather than a grounded scene grammar.
feedback.expected: Research reputable motion-direction material first, preserve a concise learning synthesis, and preregister one measurable shot plan before changing source.
feedback.evidence: The previous tactical-drop suggestion contained timing guesses and effect ideas without source evidence, while the research pass found consistent principles around staging, anticipation, timing and spacing, action-reaction, movement composition, restrained juiciness, and transform/opacity performance.
feedback.reproduction: Compare the previous effect-led suggestion with the sourced Obsidian study and its explicit three-second storyboard, rejection list, and 700px Gate checks.

feedback.observed: The faster opening improved, but the UFO then occupied the pasture while the sheep moved; sheep motion still felt awkward and flowers read as undirected dots rather than part of the scene.
feedback.expected: Let the flock own the middle act, give sheep readable turns and restrained grazing acting, and make sparse flowers recognizable at the real 700px size.
feedback.evidence: Fixed 5, 15, and 35 second frames show the UFO stationary over the action; source inspection shows repeated whole-body squash on every stationary tick, 270-degree direction values that can take the long rotation path, and flowers rendered as one colored circle plus a subpixel center.
feedback.reproduction: Render the deterministic fixture at 700px and inspect 5, 15, 35, 65, and 73 seconds, then inspect consecutive sheep turns and stationary runs.

feedback.observed: Grass could disappear before a sheep visibly arrived, sheep were about 20 percent too large, and the start of grazing lacked speed, impact, and a readable payoff.
feedback.expected: Never react before visible arrival, reduce sheep to 80 percent of the current size, and stage grazing as a brief anticipation, decisive bite, and restrained grass reaction.
feedback.evidence: The representative timeline measured grass 0.10 to 1.05 seconds ahead of visible sheep because simulation arrival ignored visual deployment delay; the grazing pose had no brace-impact body beat and matching-color crumbs were dispersed over three later chew times.
feedback.reproduction: Run the deterministic fixture and compare a representative grass cell immediately before arrival, at arrival, 80 milliseconds later, 160 milliseconds later, and during recovery; audit all first-arrival pairs mechanically.

feedback.observed: After the UFO exits, six independent nearest-target sheep repeat the same graze loop with no new event, focus transfer, or visible act progression, so changing locomotion alone would not fix the boredom.
feedback.expected: Use the learned staging principles to give the UFO-free middle act one restrained macro-event: three readable two-sheep focus transfers with speed contrast, spatial progression, and purposeful flower traces.
feedback.evidence: The v8 700px frames at 4.5, 6.2, 7.85, and 20 seconds show simultaneous undirected activity, while the planner and simulator assign every sheep by nearest reachable grass without a flock-level phase or role.
feedback.reproduction: Render v8 and the relay candidate at 700px; compare the UFO exit boundary and fixed frames at 4.40, 6.05, 7.70, and 20 seconds, then inspect target bands, launch times, flower count, and pickup start mechanically.

feedback.observed: The relay candidate improved the middle act but sheep still stopped too often, the ending lacked a memorable payoff, and the final beam had no causal relationship to a personal signature.
feedback.expected: Keep six sheep moving with a faster walk-bite-walk rhythm, then stage one game-intro-style ending in which the UFO beam visibly writes SEONARU as grass and leaves the completed image on screen.
feedback.evidence: The v9 simulation spent about 71% of sheep ticks stationary and lasted 76.00 seconds. Fixed end frames contained no identity reveal. The project-specific shot study calls for one one-more-thing setpiece, trajectory continuity, and a readable 5x7 bitmap wordmark.
feedback.reproduction: Run npm run visual:fixture; inspect one sheep across consecutive movement and grazing frames, then inspect 700px frames from beam preparation through the final hold. Run the signature, runtime, sweep, all-grass, and timing assertions.

feedback.observed: After the speed pass, sheep resumed walking before higher-level grass finished its 1.30-second disappearance, so eating and its visible result no longer belonged to the same action.
feedback.expected: Every grass level must begin reacting after visible arrival and become empty while the sheep is still performing the single bite hold.
feedback.evidence: The sheep held one 240ms tick while the grass keyframes lasted up to 1.30 seconds; the new deterministic check reproduced cells whose grass remained after departure.
feedback.reproduction: Run npm run check and inspect consecutive 700px bite frames; the all-cell assertion compares each level-specific final grass step with that sheep's next visible move.

feedback.observed: The generic frontend-design skill kept being activated even after project-specific motion research had been completed and preserved, adding context without improving the direction.
feedback.expected: Use the preserved green-movement shot contract and measured 700px frames as the motion authority; return to external or generic design guidance only when the project evidence has a named gap.
feedback.evidence: The Obsidian study now contains sourced staging, continuity, typography, timing, rejection, and Gate rules specific to this SVG, while the generic skill contributed no uncovered job in the latest pass.
feedback.reproduction: Inspect the active capability routing and the next motion candidate; frontend-design must not activate, and each motion decision must map to the project shot contract or a measured source defect.

feedback.observed: The final laser still read like thread, sheep waited after landing, flowers added clutter, a fixed flock ignored contribution density, the palette could conflict with GitHub theme, and drop positions lacked a visible reason.
feedback.expected: Scan every grass position before deployment, place a density-scaled flock at optimized locations, move each sheep immediately after landing, remove flowers, strengthen the laser silhouette, and match standard GitHub light and dark contribution palettes.
feedback.evidence: Source tracing found a fixed six-sheep cap, relay-start delays, an active flower layer, a single narrow line-like beam, fixed colors, and no pre-drop scan. Fixed 700px frames reproduced the weak causal deployment story and theme mismatch risk.
feedback.reproduction: Run npm run visual:fixture and inspect 700px light and dark frames at 0.90, 1.15, 1.48, 2.05, 4.75, 34.55, and 35.50 seconds; run density, scan, immediate-start, no-flower, theme-token, laser-sync, and runtime assertions.

feedback.observed: The v11 spotlight-like scan did not communicate analysis or placement, and the top-rail cell-by-cell laser pass made the ending feel like the worst possible mechanical plotter rather than a directed reveal.
feedback.expected: Replace the scene grammar if needed, use learned film, animation, comics, webtoon, and game-VFX principles, and produce one restrained causal opening plus a cinematic identity reveal that survives at 700px.
feedback.evidence: Fixed v11 frames showed a moving effect with no persistent decision handoff and an actor tracing 123 implementation steps. Source research converged on one idea per beat, quiet contrast, meaningful movement, previsualized eye flow, mechanic-readable VFX, audience closure, and title restraint.
feedback.reproduction: Compare v11 and v12 at 700px. Inspect 0.82, 1.20, and 1.62 seconds for scan-to-lock causality; 31.98 through 33.45 seconds for central impact, wave/cell synchronization, actor exit, and final hold; run npm run check.

feedback.observed: The bright line sweeping from above still looked cheap, the visible drop-point crosshairs looked unrelated to the pasture, and the actual sheep drop positions also felt poorly composed.
feedback.expected: Recheck the real 700px sequence, remove the rejected explanatory effects, and choose deployment positions that distribute the flock cleanly across the field.
feedback.evidence: V12 opening frames read as a barcode scanner plus game HUD. The representative points [9,5], [7,5], [26,5], [26,0], [45,0], [44,3] placed two left drops on the same lower row and did not alternate vertical weight consistently.
feedback.reproduction: Generate the fixture and inspect 700px light/dark frames from 0.64 through 4.10 seconds. Assert that no scan/lock renderer exists and that every populated horizontal band separates its paired drops vertically.

feedback.observed: The UFO movement looked chaotic and interrupted, the opening centre hold felt empty, deployment travel was slightly too fast, and the finale still looked like a generic growing circle.
feedback.expected: Use a slower continuous one-way deployment route with no unexplained centre pause, then express the final propagation through the contribution squares as a readable rectangular front and wake.
feedback.evidence: Generated keyframes exposed a three-pixel correction in the final 70ms of each flight and drop points that forced repeated vertical reversals. Fixed 700px finale frames exposed the normalized Euclidean wave as an ellipse and its white overlay as nearly invisible on the light palette.
feedback.reproduction: Run npm run visual:fixture; inspect 700px opening frames from 0.64 through 5.14 seconds and light/dark finale frames from 30.60 through 32.02 seconds; run npm run check.

feedback.observed: The final identity appeared correct for SEONARU, but the renderer did not actually connect the target GitHub account to the signature text.
feedback.expected: Each configured account should leave its own GitHub username instead of the repository author's hard-coded name.
feedback.evidence: renderGridSvg called buildSignatureCells without text and generateSvg discarded GITHUB_USERNAME after fetching the contribution calendar, so the default SEONARU was always rendered.
feedback.reproduction: Trace GITHUB_USERNAME from src/app/generateSvg.ts to renderGridSvg and buildSignatureCells; run npm run check with the 13-character compact-font assertion.

feedback.observed: The UFO should enter directly onto its first drop rather than visiting centre, and the sheep-owned middle act still needs a more entertaining but disciplined idea.
feedback.expected: Remove the centre waypoint completely and identify a middle-act improvement from measured motion rather than adding arbitrary decoration.
feedback.evidence: The opening still generated centre-to-first-drop states. Per-sheep movement keyframes contain 31–42 repeated-position stops, equal to 36–49% of visible position frames, because grazing duplicates each occupied cell before the next move.
feedback.reproduction: Inspect fixed 700px frames at 0, 0.16, 0.32, 0.48, 0.64, 0.80, and 1.04 seconds; count consecutive same-position transforms in sheep-0 through sheep-5 keyframes; run npm run check.

feedback.observed: Removing grazing holds would break the causal link between the sheep's action and disappearing grass, and the maximum flock size should not be derived from how much grass exists.
feedback.expected: Keep the stop causally readable as approach, contact, consumption, and departure, while using the same six-sheep scene budget for every non-empty contribution grid whenever six distinct assignments are feasible.
feedback.evidence: The previous suggestion optimized continuity by omitting holds but allowed grass to disappear during travel. Source inspection also showed generic stationary runs driving bite poses, even though a stationary run can be caused by collision, and buildContext used ceil(grassCount/40).
feedback.reproduction: Run npm run check; inspect the sheep head/body keyframes at each first grass step, density-cap probes from 1 through 351 active cells, and fixed 700px frames from 5.56 through 6.10 seconds.

feedback.observed: The final propagation looked like a generic expanding shape, and its physical wave behavior was questionable.
feedback.expected: Use a coherent point-wave model whose front travels at equal speed in grid space, weakens with distance, stays readable at 700px in both themes, and reveals the username at the same front without drawing a circle outline.
feedback.evidence: The previous phase function used max(abs(dx/23), abs(dy/3)), so one phase represented about 7.7 horizontal cells but one vertical cell. The final phase therefore lit complete top and bottom rows together at constant peak opacity, which was an anisotropic rectangular wipe rather than point propagation.
feedback.reproduction: Run npm run visual:fixture; inspect fixed 700px light/dark frames at 30.18, 30.28, 30.42, 30.60, 30.80, 31.00, 31.20, and 31.38 seconds; run npm run check.

feedback.observed: The grazing middle act remained repetitive even after causal bite timing; the user selected progressive fullness, one UFO airlift, stored grass energy, and a two-sheep reinforcement.
feedback.expected: Turn those choices into one causal escalation without permanently increasing the cast or adding unrelated effects.
feedback.evidence: The previous fixture kept the same six actors and repeated walk-bite-depart for most of the middle act. The corrected fixture stages four visible sheep first, relocates sheep 1 from [17,5] to [30,1] at 4.21-4.93 seconds, adds sheep 4 and 5 at 6.10 and 6.80 seconds, and maps all 201 bites to growth and energy.
feedback.reproduction: Run npm run check and npm run visual:fixture; inspect fixed 700px light/dark frames at 3.80, 4.05, 4.21, 4.37, 4.57, 4.77, 4.93, 5.20, 6.16, 6.56, 6.90, 10, and 20 seconds.

feedback.observed: The middle pickup, transport, and redrop happened so quickly that the airlift read as frantic rather than as a clear incident.
feedback.expected: Keep normal deployment speed, but give boarding, diagonal transport, and landing separate readable beats.
feedback.evidence: The first version compressed 0.16-second boarding, 0.40-second transport, and 0.16-second landing into 0.72 seconds; a 1.28-second correction still felt too fast. The current shot explicitly totals 2.40 seconds: 0.30 approach, 0.45 boarding, 1.20 transport, and 0.45 landing, with reinforcement delayed until after release.
feedback.reproduction: Run npm run check and npm run visual:fixture; inspect 700px frames at 3.91, 4.21, 4.43, 4.66, 5.26, 5.86, 6.08, 6.31, 7.54, and 8.24 seconds.

feedback.observed: GitHub identities longer than 13 characters could not be represented because generation stopped instead of producing a signature.
feedback.expected: Keep short names large, but represent longer readable identities as a centred two-line grass signature without silent truncation.
feedback.evidence: The previous renderer rejected every 14+ character value. The corrected renderer preserves 5x7 for 1-10 characters and 3x5 for 11-13, then splits 14-26 characters across two independently centred 3x3 lines. A 25-character 700px fixture spans rows 0 and 6; 27+ remains an explicit error rather than unreadable compression.
feedback.reproduction: Run npm run check; render VERY-LONG-GITHUB-USERNAME at 700px and confirm two centred lines, then confirm a 27-character value reports maximum 26 instead of truncating.

feedback.observed: A fixed six-sheep cast and one final group pickup flatten the visible difference between developers with roughly 100 and 300 contribution cells, while waiting for every sheep to finish makes the grazing act feel idle.
feedback.expected: Scale simultaneous staffing as 1, 2, 4, or 6 sheep, exchange each full sheep immediately without lowering the working headcount, and show every required sheep in a two-row StarCraft-style panel with selected status and individual fullness.
feedback.evidence: The corrected deterministic fixture uses six working slots, partitions their 201 causal bites into 28 visible roster sheep, performs 22 serialized exchanges, and keeps the complete roster readable at 700px without a 12-sheep cap. Separate 100- and 300-cell probes expose 22 and 62 roster sheep respectively.
feedback.reproduction: Run npm run check and npm run visual:fixture; inspect 700px dark frames at 4.84, 5.08, 5.18, 15.00, 28.00, and 35.50 seconds, plus contribution-energy staffing probes and an empty grid.

feedback.observed: The accepted command panel looked crude: the enlarged field sprite became a distorted white blob, 6-7px monospaced headers were hard to read, and 16px roster slots clustered on the left while leaving unused space.
feedback.expected: Keep the two-row full roster and live information, but make the selected sheep recognizable, give the header a clear hierarchy, and distribute roster sheep cleanly across the available width at both 28 and 62 members.
feedback.evidence: The reported 700px frame showed a 44x35 enlargement of the 16x13 field glyph, fixed 16px roster pitch, small undifferentiated header type, and a large empty area to the right of the 28-member roster. The corrected frames keep the original sheep at 28x23 only in the selected card, use 8.5px label/value typography, and replace repeated miniatures with a full-width numbered selection grid and individual progress bars.
feedback.reproduction: Run npm run visual:fixture; inspect 700px light/dark frames at 5.08, 15.00, and 35.50 seconds, then render the deterministic 300-cell probe and inspect its 62-member roster at 20.00 and 57.50 seconds.

feedback.observed: A full sheep and its hungry replacement appeared in the same place without a readable separation, so the exchange looked like one sheep being lifted and returned. The final six sheep also waited motionless until the whole field finished before pickup began.
feedback.expected: Make each exchange read as an outgoing sheep followed by a different incoming sheep, and begin collecting finished final sheep while the remaining sheep are still eating.
feedback.evidence: Source tracing found a direct opacity crossfade with no empty frame and a final pickup cursor explicitly clamped to the latest sheep finish. The corrected fixture inserts an 80ms empty slot, changes selection from SHEEP 01 to SHEEP 07, and begins the first final pickup at 27.10 seconds while grass is still 90 percent instead of waiting for the 28.54-second last finish.
feedback.reproduction: Run npm run visual:fixture; inspect 700px dark frames at 4.84, 5.04, 5.17, 5.27, 27.10, 27.84, 28.76, and 31.16 seconds.

feedback.observed: The profile README still shows the pre-panel SVG, the card follows the operating-system color preference instead of the GitHub theme selected by the viewer, and the command panel does not separate its left and right jobs strongly enough.
feedback.expected: Publish the complete panel to the profile README, select a light or dark SVG from the viewer's GitHub theme, and frame the selected-unit and flock-roster areas as two unmistakable sections.
feedback.evidence: The public SeoNaRu/SeoNaRu asset is the old 468,854-byte, 700x115 SVG with no flock-panel, while the accepted local asset is 991,057 bytes and 700x206 with the panel. The latest successful scheduled workflow predates v21. Source inspection also shows an OS-only prefers-color-scheme rule, a dark command panel even in the light palette, and only thin separator lines between panel jobs.
feedback.reproduction: Compare the public profile asset metadata and README image URL with the generated fixture; inspect forced 700px light and dark panel frames at 5.27, 15.00, and 27.84 seconds.

proposals.change_target: product code and its deterministic SVG regression check
proposals.cause: Actor count, duplicated secondary animation tracks, and whole-group linear transforms flatten the motion hierarchy and consume the visual budget needed for character acting.
proposals.candidate_change: Cap the flock at eight, add nested landing/walk/graze/pickup poses, activate UFO banking and hover, simplify the UFO art, and share sparse flower and crumb animations.
proposals.discovery_evidence: The user correction and frozen benchmark identify motion hierarchy, character acting, easing, cohesion, and README readability as the causal quality dimensions.
proposals.reproduction: Render the deterministic 53x7 fixture at 700px and compare fixed frames at entry, grazing, pickup, and completion.
proposals.primary_metric: Frozen visual benchmark score out of 20, target at least 16 with no dimension below 3.
proposals.prediction: A single hero actor plus eight or fewer characterful sheep will make the narrative readable while shared secondary motion removes visual and rendering noise.
proposals.falsification_condition: Reject if any benchmark dimension stays below 3, the total stays below 16, npm run check fails, or SVG size exceeds the recorded 15% guardrail.
proposals.regression_check: npm run check plus fixed 700px frames at entry, grazing, pickup, and completion.
proposals.transfer_check: Not applicable; this is a project-scoped task candidate with no personal or core transfer claim.
guardrails: npm run check
No NaN or undefined SVG values
Four to eight sheep in the representative fixture
No network, credential, deployment, or publication permission expansion
Representative SVG no larger than 4,714,129 bytes
proposals.rollback: Restore the pre-candidate motion and rendering source while retaining the feedback record.

proposals.cause: The rejected candidate spent its motion budget on ambient wobble and 3D distortion while long travel, spawn, grazing, and pickup intervals kept the actual narrative slow.
proposals.candidate_change: Restore the original UFO, remove hover and 3D banking, cap the flock at six, accelerate UFO travel with a strong ease-out, shorten spawn spacing, and compress sheep, grazing, pickup, entry, and exit timing.
proposals.discovery_evidence: User review directly prefers the original glyph and identifies higher speed plus six sheep as the desired correction; fixed frames reproduce the cheap wobble and slow total rhythm.
proposals.reproduction: Render the same deterministic 53x7 fixture at 700px and inspect consecutive frames across the first UFO travel plus entry, grazing, and pickup frames.
proposals.primary_metric: User or independent visual Gate accepts UFO shape and motion rhythm with exactly six sheep; npm run check passes.
proposals.prediction: Moving faster only during purposeful travel, then stopping cleanly, will feel more premium than continuous hover while reducing total runtime by at least 35% from the rejected 139.51-second candidate.
proposals.falsification_condition: Reject if the original UFO is not restored, the representative fixture does not contain exactly six sheep, runtime exceeds 90 seconds, motion still reads as floating or cheap at 700px, or npm run check fails.
proposals.regression_check: npm run check, deterministic fixture runtime and sheep-count assertions, and fixed 700px consecutive UFO-travel frames.
proposals.transfer_check: Not applicable; this is a project-scoped visual candidate.
guardrails: npm run check
Exactly six sheep in the representative fixture
No ufo-hover or ufo-bank animation
Representative runtime no more than 90 seconds
No permission expansion
proposals.rollback: Restore the rejected candidate source only for comparison; do not reactivate it without new visual evidence.

proposals.change_target: UFO rotation and movement keyframes
proposals.cause: Direction was removed to avoid cheap spinning, and pickup travel had no explicit departure keyframe, so the glyph faced down and position interpolation created a long slow drift.
proposals.candidate_change: Use shortest-path directional headings, turn during the final 100 milliseconds before departure, hold the heading through flight, and add explicit stationary pickup departure keyframes.
proposals.discovery_evidence: User review identified the downward-facing flight; source and generated-keyframe inspection exposed both the fixed zero-degree rotation and the missing pickup departure hold.
proposals.reproduction: Render the deterministic 53x7 fixture at 700px and inspect the first rightward flight plus the 60-second pickup-wait frame.
proposals.primary_metric: Every purposeful flight points toward its destination before translation and pickup waiting has zero position drift; npm run check passes.
proposals.prediction: A staged turn, fast flight, and precise stop will read as intentional direction changes without adding trails, shake, hover, or banking.
proposals.falsification_condition: Reject if the first rightward departure is not at -90 degrees, pickup waiting drifts, ambient hover or banking returns, or npm run check fails.
proposals.regression_check: npm run check plus fixed 700px frames during the first flight and at 60 seconds.
proposals.transfer_check: Not applicable; this is a project-scoped visual candidate.
guardrails: npm run check
Exactly six sheep in the representative fixture
No ufo-hover or ufo-bank animation
Representative runtime no more than 90 seconds
No permission expansion
proposals.rollback: Restore the v3 fixed heading and pickup movement only for comparison; keep the accepted six-sheep timing and original UFO glyph.

proposals.change_target: motion-direction discovery and preregistration procedure
proposals.cause: The Coach jumped from visual symptoms to implementation effects without first grounding the scene in established motion language or a measurable storyboard.
proposals.candidate_change: Before future motion source edits, review reputable material across animation, game feel, film movement and editing, and web performance; write one 700px storyboard with numeric timing, a single primary-action budget, a rejection list, performance boundaries, and falsifiable Gate questions.
proposals.discovery_evidence: The user explicitly required a learning pass; nine video lessons and five research or official references converged on staging, timing and spacing, anticipation, action-reaction, contrast, restrained embellishment, and compositor-friendly SVG motion.
proposals.reproduction: Compare the unsourced tactical-drop suggestion with the Obsidian research page, which records the evidence, three-second shot table, numeric motion contract, forbidden effects, and post-implementation Gate checklist.
proposals.primary_metric: The next motion candidate has one sourced and measurable 700px shot contract before any source edit, and the user or independent visual Gate accepts its direction as specific rather than generic or effect-led.
proposals.prediction: Research-first staging will reduce repeated visual rejection by making timing, hierarchy, and effect restraint explicit before implementation begins.
proposals.falsification_condition: Reject if the next candidate starts source work without the shot contract, bundles unrelated effects, lacks 700px performance and reduced-motion boundaries, or is still rejected as generic despite following the recorded plan.
proposals.regression_check: Validate evolution state, confirm the Obsidian page contains sources, storyboard, numeric contract, forbidden list, and Gate questions, then run the repository check only after later source changes.
proposals.transfer_check: Not applicable; this is a project-scoped Coach procedure with no personal or core transfer claim.
guardrails: No product source change during the research pass
No copyrighted video transcript or copied course material in the wiki
One primary action and at most one supporting reaction per beat
Evaluate at 700px with reduced-motion and SVG performance boundaries
No publication, deployment, credential, or network-write expansion
permission_delta: Write the requested synthesis to the user-designated local Obsidian vault
proposals.rollback: Remove the research-first proposal from active consideration if it fails the next visual Gate; retain the sourced wiki page as project research rather than accepted procedure.

proposals.change_target: UFO travel keyframes, deployment timeline, and deterministic SVG regression check
proposals.cause: UFO translation was faster than before, but 1.98-second simulation spawn gaps and sheep-walk-coupled departures still made the six-drop opening read as a slow sequence of independent stops.
proposals.candidate_change: Decouple UFO departure from sheep walking, deploy six sheep in one sub-four-second passage, and stage each flight as pre-turn, accelerated travel, three-pixel overshoot, 70-millisecond settle, and one travel-only streak.
proposals.discovery_evidence: The preregistered Obsidian shot contract calls for anticipation, 180-320 millisecond travel, 50-80 millisecond impact, two-to-three-pixel overshoot, and at most one supporting reaction; source tracing located the pacing bottleneck in spawn and release scheduling rather than glyph speed alone.
proposals.reproduction: Run npm run visual:fixture and inspect the 700px fixture from 0.8 to 3.8 seconds, including a frame during a rightward flight and the sixth sheep landing.
proposals.primary_metric: A fresh visual Gate accepts pacing and hierarchy at 700px; all six sheep are visible by four seconds and npm run check passes.
proposals.prediction: Removing the hidden scheduling waits while keeping one restrained speed cue will make the opening feel like one directed game-intro passage rather than six UI transitions.
proposals.falsification_condition: Reject if the opening still feels mechanical or cheap at 700px, any departure drifts before its actual start, the streak competes with the UFO, all six sheep are not visible by four seconds, runtime exceeds 80 seconds, or npm run check fails.
proposals.regression_check: npm run check plus fixed 700px frames at 0.9, 1.6, 2.6, and 3.7 seconds.
proposals.transfer_check: Not applicable; this is a project-scoped visual candidate.

Exactly six sheep in the representative fixture
All six sheep visible by four seconds
No ufo-hover, ufo-bank, blur, filter, or camera shake
One streak element visible only during purposeful travel
prefers-reduced-motion hides nonessential streak, ripple, crumb, and flower motion
Representative runtime no more than 80 seconds
No permission expansion
proposals.rollback: Restore the v4 travel constants, six-tick spawn spacing, sheep-walk-coupled UFO release, and non-overshooting movement keyframes while retaining the research record.

proposals.change_target: UFO stage lifecycle, sheep pose and heading keyframes, flower silhouette, and deterministic SVG regression check
proposals.cause: The scene had no act boundary after deployment, stationary sheep reused a full-body tick pulse, direction angles could interpolate along the long arc, and a single-circle flower lost its identity at README size.
proposals.candidate_change: Exit the UFO immediately after deployment and re-enter from offstage for pickup; use shortest-path sheep headings, walking bounce only during travel, one head nod per multi-tick stop, and sparse four-petal flowers with a quiet scale reveal.
proposals.discovery_evidence: The user's mid-scene correction is reproduced in fixed frames, and the source paths isolate one lifecycle omission, one rotation defect, one repeated-pose defect, and one silhouette defect rather than a need for more effects.
proposals.reproduction: Run npm run visual:fixture; compare 700px frames at 3.7, 4.0, 15, 35, 65, 73.0, and 73.4 seconds and inspect consecutive sheep heading values.
proposals.primary_metric: A fresh visual Gate accepts mid-scene hierarchy, sheep acting, and flower readability at 700px; npm run check passes.
